# Synapse 2.0.11

A small release: agent turns cost less where a provider caches only what is marked, Claude Haiku 5.5 thinks at the effort you pick, Synapse AI says when a model is too small for it, and Synapse reads the real size of Bedrock's older Mistral models and of GPT-6.

## Changed

- **Agent turns are cached where the provider needs them marked.** Some providers cache a prompt only where the caller marks it: a model gateway (the `synapse.` models), OpenRouter's Claude models, and five of OpenRouter's Qwen models (Qwen3 Max, Qwen Plus, Qwen3.6 Plus, Qwen3 Coder Plus and Qwen3 Coder Flash). Synapse sent them plain text, so each turn of an agent paid full price again for the same instructions and conversation. Each agent turn is now sent with its prompt marked, so what repeats from one turn to the next is read from the cache at a fraction of the price. The words sent are the same, character for character. Other model calls (a model step, an evaluator, Knowledge) and every other provider are sent exactly as before.
- **Cache markers for an OpenAI-compatible server.** Settings → Models → OpenAI-compatible has a new **Send prompt cache markers** box, off by default. Tick it for a server that passes Anthropic-style cache markers on, such as LiteLLM in front of Claude, and agent turns sent to it are marked the same way. Leave it off for a server that doesn't take them.
- **Claude Haiku 5.5 thinks as the rest of Claude 5 does.** On your own Anthropic key, Haiku 5.5 now gets adaptive thinking at the effort you pick, as Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 do. It always thinks, so Off runs it at its lowest level. Haiku 4.5 is unchanged.
- **GPT-6 is read at 272,000 tokens.** GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 hold about a million tokens, but on Bedrock a request with more than 272,000 input tokens is billed at a higher rate, so each step keeps its inputs under that.

## Fixed

- **Bedrock's older Mistral models are read at their real size.** Synapse read Bedrock's Mistral Large 24.02 as Mistral's own 128,000-token model, so it could give that model work it refuses: it holds 32,768 tokens. Mistral Large 24.02, Mistral Small 24.02, Mistral 7B Instruct and Mixtral 8x7B on Bedrock now read 32,768 tokens, so model picks and each step's room for its inputs see them as they are. Mistral Large 2 and the `-latest` names keep their sizes.
- **Synapse AI never offers a stronger model too small for it.** When a Synapse AI turn fails and it offers to try again on a stronger model, or offers to move to one, it no longer suggests a model known to hold too little for its long planning prompt. The stronger model you can choose on a plan card follows the same rule for an agent that reads long inputs. A model whose size isn't known is still offered.
- **Synapse AI says when a model is too small for it.** Synapse AI needs a model that reads at least 128K tokens. On a smaller one (a local qwen3 8B, say) it now says so before it starts and names one that fits (`ollama pull llama3.1`), instead of failing part-way; the first-run Ollama tip suggests llama3.1 now too.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.11`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
